evidence: src/infrastructure/task-controller.ts: the TaskController constructor registers Express routes with this.router.post/get, which is transport work belonging to infrastructure
createTask/listTasks check status with isTaskStatus imported from the domain, so the rule is delegated rather than restated
createUser/createProject/createTask/listTasks/markDone each only call a TaskService method and serialize the result with res.json
readString/requiredString/requiredParam only check the shape of HTTP input
errorHandler maps DomainError to 400, NotFoundError to 404 and anything else to 500, which is transport error translation
Borderline: readString(req.body, "id") ?? randomUUID() supplies a default id in the controller; this is acceptable at the edge but could belong in the application layer
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file is an Express HTTP adapter, and everything in it fits the infrastructure (transport) layer. It registers routes, parses and checks the shape of request bodies, params and query strings, delegates every use case to the injected TaskService, and maps errors to HTTP status codes. The status check calls the domain predicate isTaskStatus rather than restating the allowed values, so the business rule stays in the domain. Two borderline points: the controller supplies a default id with randomUUID(), and it throws DomainError for missing request fields. Generating a fallback id at the edge is acceptable, though the application layer arguably should own it. Using DomainError for malformed input conflates error categories, but it is not a business rule placed in the wrong layer. No persistence logic, domain rules or use-case orchestration is implemented here.
